title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations along Waltham corridors in Bentley University’s practical orbit, each paired with one directly sourced reason to go.

cards.entity_name: Charles River Museum of Industry & Innovation
cards.title: See Waltham’s Industrial Story
cards.subtitle: Moody Street corridor — museum exhibits
cards.notes: Head to 154 Moody Street with a student ID for reduced admission, and confirm hours before visiting because private events can affect access.
cards.short_summary: A Moody Street museum connecting machinery, innovation, and Waltham’s watchmaking history.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is at 154 Moody Street and offers $5 admission to college students with current ID.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Friday 10:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. and Saturday 10:00 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; final admission is 30 minutes before closing. Hours may change for special or private events.

cards.title: Choose an Ice-Cream Break
cards.subtitle: Moody Street corridor — year-round parlor
cards.notes: Walk to 367 Moody Street for ice cream, frozen yogurt, vegan options, pastries, coffee, or tea; check the shop page before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A year-round Moody Street stop with frozen desserts and café choices.
cards.evidence_claim: Lizzy’s operates a year-round parlor at 367 Moody Street offering ice cream, frozen yogurt, vegan ice cream, pastries, espresso, coffee, and tea.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists noon–10:00 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and noon–10:30 p.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Catch a First-Run Film
cards.subtitle: Pine Street block beside Moody Street — independent cinema
cards.notes: Check the current film listing, then find the twin-screen cinema at 16 Pine Street; the box office opens shortly before the first show.
cards.short_summary: An independent two-screen theater showing films from indie productions to major releases.
cards.evidence_claim: Embassy Theater is an independent twin-screen cinema at 16 Pine Street showing first-run independent films and Hollywood releases.
cards.access_notes: The box office opens 30 minutes before the first show; consult the current event or film listing before visiting.

cards.title: Browse Beyond Campus
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — public library
cards.notes: Visit the library at 735 Main Street for community information and collections; review its directions, parking, and policy links before arrival.
cards.short_summary: Waltham’s Main Street public-library hub for informational, educational, and recreational resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Waltham Public Library is located at 735 Main Street and identifies itself as a community hub offering informational, educational, and recreational resources.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s linked Hours, Directions & Parking page to confirm building access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Pizzi Farm Market, Deli & Ice Cream Shoppe
cards.title: Pair Lunch with a Cone
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Street corridor — market, deli, and creamery
cards.notes: Stop at 495 Lincoln Street for a deli meal or frozen treat, and consult the seasonal schedule because each counter keeps different hours.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding Lincoln Street market combining a deli with a seasonal ice-cream window.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizzi Farm at 495 Lincoln Street operates a market, deli, and ice-cream shop offering sandwiches, panini, salads, soup, cones, and sundaes.
cards.access_notes: Market, deli, and ice-cream hours differ and the ice-cream schedule changes seasonally; check the official page before leaving.

cards.title: Follow a Wooded Trail
cards.subtitle: Totten Pond Road corridor — hiking and vistas
cards.notes: Start at 314 Totten Pond Road for wooded trails and scenic viewpoints; bring the official park map and use only designated picnic sites.
cards.short_summary: A large natural park offering marked hiking terrain, viewpoints, and designated picnic areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Hill Park at 314 Totten Pond Road covers 273.07 acres and contains wooded hiking trails, scenic vistas, and designated picnic sites.
cards.access_notes: The seasonal vehicle-access road opens daily at 10:00 a.m.; consult the city page and park map for current access rules.

cards.entity_name: Stonehurst, The Robert Treat Paine Estate
cards.title: Walk a Historic Estate Landscape
cards.subtitle: Robert Treat Paine Drive corridor — landmark grounds
cards.notes: Call before heading to 100 Robert Treat Paine Drive, since private rentals close the immediate grounds and guided tours require appointments.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark estate with year-round landscape access when private events permit.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonehurst is a historic landmark at 100 Robert Treat Paine Drive; its grounds open year-round from sunrise to sunset, while guided tours are appointment-only.
cards.source_title: Stonehurst, The Robert Treat Paine Estate | Waltham, MA
cards.access_notes: Grounds normally open sunrise to sunset, but the estate closes during private rentals. Call ahead; guided tours require an appointment.

cards.title: Tour a Federal-Era Estate
cards.subtitle: Lyman Street corridor — mansion, gardens, and greenhouses
cards.notes: Plan a first- or third-Saturday visit to 185 Lyman Street, or walk the grounds during public hours; check for private-event closures first.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark pairing a Federal-style mansion with gardens and historic greenhouses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lyman Estate at 185 Lyman Street is a 1793 National Historic Landmark with a mansion, preserved gardens, historic greenhouses, and 37 acres.
cards.access_notes: House tours are offered on the first and third Saturdays; grounds are generally open dawn to dusk but close during private rentals.

cards.title: Explore a Museum and Working Farm
cards.subtitle: Gore Street corridor — mansion, farm, and open grounds
cards.notes: Use 52 Gore Street for the entrance, explore the grounds between dawn and dusk, and check the calendar before adding a mansion tour or program.
cards.short_summary: A nineteenth-century estate combining a museum, working farm, and extensive public green space.
cards.evidence_claim: Gore Place at 52 Gore Street includes a nineteenth-century mansion museum, 50 acres of green space, and a working farm; its grounds are free to visit.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are free and open dawn to dusk daily unless a special event is underway. Mansion tours and some programs require paid tickets.

cards.entity_name: Mass Central Rail Trail — Waltham Segment
cards.title: Take the Shared-Use Trail West
cards.subtitle: Beaver Street corridor — Waltham rail-trail access
cards.notes: Join the named Waltham segment near Beaver Street for an off-road walk or ride, and consult the state status page before attempting longer connections.
cards.short_summary: A three-mile Waltham shared-use segment within the developing regional trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: The state reports that Waltham completed a three-mile Mass Central Rail Trail segment from Beaver Street to Route 117/Hillside Road in 2023.
cards.access_notes: Review the state project-status page before traveling because connecting segments remain in different stages of completion.
